g.text: The last hour is already taken
Half of adults are on a screen in bed every day.
Another third are there most days or several days a week; a
quarter choose the phone over sleep.
Each extra hour of it costs 24 minutes of sleep.
One more hour of screen time after getting into bed raised the
odds of insomnia symptoms by 59 percent.
A book in bed does the opposite.
In a randomised trial, 42 percent of people who read in bed said
their sleep improved, against 28 percent who did not.
Sources: American Academy of Sleep Medicine, 2,007 US adults, June 2025; SHOT2022 in Frontiers in Psychiatry, 45,202 students,
March 2025; The People's Trial in Trials 22:873, 991 participants, 2021.
